item.title: From Abu Dhabi to Dublin via Moscow: peace talks and a row over who speaks for Europe
item.description: Good morning. I’m Luca Bertuzzi, holding the pen for today’s newsletter. In this edition, leaders from across the world are flocking to Dublin for the European Political Community summit, where the war in Ukraine looms large, while the latest EU-UK draft statement significantly softened its wording.

item.title: Video shows soldier reprimanding Hegseth and advisers at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
item.description: A soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in Arlington tells US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and his group to maintain silence and respect after they take photos and are heard laughing.

item.title: Spain grinds to a halt in first general strike in 14 years
item.description: Riot police clashed with masked protesters in Madrid and Barcelona, leaving more than 70 people arrested, as unions and employers gave opposing verdicts on the walkout.

item.title: Nvidia board weighs Jensen Huang’s future as reports emerge of second affair
item.description: The report of a second affair follows Huang admitting to having a relationship with Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed.

item.title: Europe Today: Ukraine talks yield prisoner swap as European leaders meet in Dublin
item.description: European leaders gather in Dublin for the European Political Community summit after two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi produced a prisoner exchange but no ceasefire. US envoys head to Moscow, then to Zelenskyy. We also hear from the EU justice chief Michael McGrath and look at COP31.

item.title: EU household electricity and gas prices fell in the first half of 2026: Who pays the most?
item.description: Household electricity and gas prices in the EU fell in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025. Prices rose in many European capitals in October, and households could face higher bills in early 2027.

item.title: Moment historic SS United States sinks off Florida’s coast
item.description: The historic SS United States, once the fastest ship on the seas, made a slow final journey beneath the waters Wednesday.

item.title: This free habit could boost your child’s mental health
item.description: Regular trips to the park from birth to age 11 are linked to better mental health and social skills in children, a new study has found.

item.title: ‘Treasures for the entire planet’: Scientists map life in one of the world’s last wild ecosystems
item.description: Scientists are mapping one of the world’s last wild ecosystems to help us ‘understand what we have lost elsewhere’.

item.title: Happy Passports Index revealed: Where does your country rank?
item.description: The Happy Passports Index ranks 50 countries on everything from life satisfaction and civil liberties to passport strength and income, and the results are surprising.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 12th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 12th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: At least two dead while others are trapped in the rubble after a building collapse in New York City
item.description: One resident of the collapsed building, Anderson Velez, recounted that he was at work when his wife phoned and said that their two children, aged 2 and 7, were among those trapped in the rubble, local media reported.

item.title: Spain: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after peaceful general strike march
item.description: Burning barricades and clashes with riot police erupted in Barcelona after a peaceful march against soaring housing costs. Police used projectiles to disperse masked protesters as violence spread through the city centre.

item.title: Spain: 120,000 brave rain to demand affordable housing and better wages
item.description: Around 120,000 demonstrators marched through central Madrid on Wednesday 11 November, according to authorities, as Spain's first nationwide general strike since 2012 brought crowds onto the streets to protest against soaring housing costs and mounting pressure on household budgets.

item.title: France's 11 November ceremonies: Macron, Le Pen, Mélenchon between memory and pacifism
item.description: Marking the 108th anniversary of the 1918 armistice, Emmanuel Macron led the ceremony at the Arc de Triomphe, while Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon chose symbolic venues to deliver their messages months before the presidential election.

item.title: German ministries spend €5.8 million on office décor, drawing taxpayers' criticism
item.description: Citizens face burdens and service cuts, while the federal government spends millions on furniture, lamps and decor, claims the Taxpayers' Association.

item.title: Zaporizhzhia mayor: city lives in constant fear as Russian attacks continue
item.description: Few places in Ukraine suffer more from Russia's invasion. Zaporizhzhia mayor Regina Kharchenko tells Euronews about winter, attacks on civilians and the Russian-held nuclear plant.

item.title: Is the EU setting the right priorities? MEPs slug it out on The Ring
item.description: In this edition of our debate show, MEPs Benedetta Scuderi (Greens) from Italy and Markus Ferber (EPP) from Germany go face-to-face on the defining issue in the EU.

item.title: German tech company signs €60 million contract with Elon Musk for satellite solar cell supply
item.description: SpaceX signed a €60 million deal with German mechanical engineering company Singulus Technologies for the strategic supply of solar cells, giving the German company a massive price jump.

item.title: Russian ambassador to the US dies after a year and a half in the job
item.description: Alexander Darchiev was apointed to the role of Russia's ambassador to the United States soon after US President Donald Trump returned to power.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 11th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 11th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Trinidad and Tobago highest court overturns gay sex ban
item.description: The island nation's highest court overturned a 1986 law criminalising consensual sexual relations between adults of the same sex.

item.title: Portugal closes all schools and non-essential services over Storm Charles
item.description: It was the first time in living memory that Portugal’s roughly 8,000 schools had cancelled classes nationwide due to a forecast storm.

item.title: We should 'salute' Ukraine for military campaign against Russian diesel infrastructure
item.description: NATO is involved in US-convened talks in Abu Dhabi about the future security settlement for Europe as part once the Russia - Ukrainian war ends. NATO's Supreme Allied Commander says it remains to be seen whether Russian President Putin is serious about peace.

item.title: Finland approves Tesla assisted driving cars ahead of EU vote
item.description: Finland has given Tesla the green light to use its assisted driving technology on its vehicles, but the system still needs EU-wide approval before it can be rolled out across the bloc.

item.title: EU targets subscription traps, addictive design and hidden fees with new digital rules
item.description: The European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act would introduce new protections against unfair online commercial practices, alongside a separate enforcement reform that could see companies fined up to 6% of their annual global turnover.

item.title: Russia bars four French figures over expulsion of Xenia Fedorova
item.description: One of those targeted says the ban is "recognition" of his work against foreign interference, while the EU accuses the former RT France chief of spreading Kremlin talking points on French television.

item.title: A Portuguese group will manufacture components for Swedish Saab fighter jets
item.description: A Swedish company announced a partnership with Portuguese industrial group Vangest to produce eight complex parts in Portugal for Gripen E/F fighters. The Swedish jet is among the options to renew the Portuguese Air Force's F-16 fleet.

item.title: How ancient nomadic survival skills became global sporting events
item.description: Horseback wrestling, endurance racing, archery and traditional games grew from the skills of nomadic life. At the World Nomad Games, those traditions now draw athletes from more than 100 countries.

item.title: Exploring Uzbekistan’s silk road soul, from Tashkent metro to Samarkand
item.description: From ancient Silk Road cities and magnificent architecture to vibrant bazaars and rich traditions, join Lilly Douse as she discovers the history, culture and flavours of Uzbekistan.

item.title: EES errors could see thousands of travellers incorrectly flagged as overstayers. Here’s what to do
item.description: Some travellers are facing issues with their exit from the Schengen zone being missed, leading to the system incorrectly suggesting they have violated the 90 days in any 180-day period rule.

item.title: French journalist Christophe Gleizes marks 500 days in Algerian prison, as loved ones urge presidential pardon
item.description: French sports journalist Christophe Gleizes was sentenced to seven years in prison by Algerian authorities, amid tensions between Paris and Algiers.

item.title: Storm Charles: Heavy rain and strong winds batter Portugal
item.description: Heavy rain, rough seas and strong winds hit Costa da Caparica in Portugal, with coastal facilities closed and streets left waterlogged.

item.title: EU plans Doha defence talks to strengthen security ties with Gulf countries
item.description: EU Ambassador to Qatar Antonino Maggiore tells Euronews that Europe plans to strengthen defence cooperation with Qatar and the Gulf countries, as "every crisis brings opportunities," while also deepening political and economic cooperation with the region.

item.title: Has Europe managed to attract researchers escaping US academia under Trump? | Euronews Tech Talks Talks
item.description: Over the past year, Europe has tried to attract researchers who no longer feel comfortable working in the United States’ academic system under the Donald Trump administration due to budget cuts and policy shifts. But did it succeed?

item.title: ECB says Lagarde's exit will not delay the digital euro as Brussels negotiates the law
item.description: Christine Lagarde's early departure will not delay the digital euro, a European Central Bank official stated at the Web Summit in Lisbon, citing the pilot due next year and a pledge by Brussels to agree the law by the end of 2026, while dismissing fears the project threatens people's privacy.

item.title: Over 60% of women in German military are sexually harassed, study finds
item.description: More than half of all female Bundeswehr soldiers have already experienced sexual misconduct, a hidden-figure study shows, revealing up to five times more cases than officially reported.

item.title: Abu Dhabi peace talks end with prisoner exchange agreement as US envoys prepare to meet Putin
item.description: A large-scale prisoner exchange emerged as the only tangible result of two days of US-mediated talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi, with no breakthrough on a ceasefire or territorial disputes. Kushner told Euronews that "we are pushing a boulder uphill" for a Putin-Zelenskyy meeting.

item.title: Princess Diana’s iconic ‘Revenge Dress’ goes on display ahead of auction
item.description: Princess Diana’s iconic ‘Revenge Dress’ is on display at Sotheby’s in Geneva ahead of its first auction in nearly 30 years.

item.title: Santorini seeks year-round tourism by promoting gastronomy, wine and culture
item.description: The popular Aegean island, having first regulated cruise tourism, is now implementing a plan to increase winter arrivals by promoting activities beyond the famous sunset over the Caldera.

item.title: EU lawmakers push to reduce Europe's dependence on foreign cloud providers
item.description: The Cloud and AI Development Act should give Europe greater control over essential technologies while helping its own tech industry grow and compete globally, say MEPs.

item.title: Protesters outside Israel’s Knesset oppose Arab lawmakers, call for new elections
item.description: Demonstrators gathered outside Israel’s parliament in Jerusalem, calling for new elections and expressing opposition to the presence and role of Arab lawmakers in the Knesset.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang helped unleash AI slop - now it's coming for him
item.description: If his extramarital affair becoming public knowledge wasn't bad enough, now Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has to confront a tidal wave of AI-generated memes.

item.title: The 500 best bars in the world have been revealed – and 13 of the top 25 are in Europe
item.description: From a bar distillery in Oslo to a speakeasy behind a pastrami shop in Barcelona, these are the spots you need to know about.

item.title: 'No longer science fiction': Flying cars could launch in China in months, says Xpeng
item.description: "It’s no longer science fiction or just a single demo aircraft," Michael Du, vice president and chief financial officer of Chinese company XPeng, told Euronews Next.

item.title: 'Our final, most soul-destroying humiliation': Nick Cave issues warning about AI-generated music
item.description: Nick Cave has shared his thoughts on the use of AI in music and songwriting, calling song generator platforms "indicators of this nascent technology’s demonic potential to hollow out human endeavour and sever our connection to the divine."

item.title: Russia’s last openly critical newspaper Novaya Gazeta shuts its Moscow office
item.description: The paper said security services and censors forced it to stop operating after they evicted it, shut down its donation system, blocked its printing, and revoked its media registration.

item.title: Schools in Italy, Ireland and UK evacuated after hoax bomb threats that also target Meloni
item.description: Italian ministers suspect a deliberate strategy to spread fear, after similar hoaxes hit schools in Britain and Ireland and media outlets in Bulgaria.

item.title: ‘A restless and difficult night’ in the Baltics as NATO fighter jets fail to shoot down drone
item.description: Four drones and dozens of suspected meteorological balloon sightings were detected moving from Belarus towards NATO's external border.

item.title: Four Seasons is launching a new private jet trip around the world – here's what guests can expect
item.description: The 23-day trip will take just 48 guests from San Francisco to Seoul, Sri Lanka, Zanzibar, Egypt and the French Riviera, with private yacht excursions, exclusive cultural experiences and stays at some of the world's most luxurious hotels.
